verdict.rationale: Epic's license page explicitly grants 'Access to the source code' and docs describe creating new Gameplay C++ classes that recompile directly into the Editor, and community comments corroborate 'source code included.' Missing for 10: independent hands-on account of actually patching core engine internals (not just gameplay classes), and the probe notes the source repo is EULA/GitHub-account gated rather than freely open, which adds friction to the 'when I hit a wall' scenario.
